To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GABA A receptor agonist musimol and antagonist bicucullin in the PnOr of mice modulate sleep, cortical EEG activity, ACh release in PnOr, breathing and recovery time from anesthesia.

microinjection of muscimol (a GABAA receptor positive allosteric modulator) into the PnOrt increased the amount of time that mice spent in the wakefulness state, and this effect was reversed by microinjection of the GABAA antagonist bicucullin.

microinjection of the GABAA agonist musciminol into the pontine reticula nucleus oralis increases wakefulness, decreases rapid eye movement and non-REM sleep, and increases electroencephalographic power in the delta (0.5-4 Hz) frequency range during wakefulness and the theta (4-9 Hz) frequency range in REM sleep in mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidation of the neural mechanisms that regulate the five phenotypes of wakefulness, sleep, and general anesthesia.
the role of the pontine reticulata in the modulation of arousal.
the role of GABA receptors in the pontomedullary reticular formation (PMRF) in modulating arousal states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GABAA receptors modulate arousal and that their activation in the PnOR promotes wakefulness and decreases NREM and REM sleep.
GABAA Receptors are involved in the control of the sleep/wake cycle and in the regulation of ACh release, respiration and recovery from anesthesia.
GABAA receptor activation in the PnOR promotes wakefulness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GABAA receptor activation in the pontine oral part of the brainstem promotes wakefulness and that the effects of GABAergic drugs on wakefulness are mediated by GABAA receptors.
GABAA receptor activation in the PnOR promotes wakefulness and GABAergic transmission may underlie paradoxical behavioral activation.
the GABAergic system in the PnOR is involved in the modulation of sleep-wake cycle and anesthesia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PnO is a key structure in the brain for modulating arousal.
the GABAA receptors on the cholinergic neurons in the PnORF play a role in the modulation of arousal and anesthesia.
the PnO is an important site for the regulation of arousal, and that the PnOR is a site where the effects of benzodiazepine receptor agonists are mediated.
